verdicts.note: Encoding facts hold and are stronger than stated: on iOS live scanning (AVCaptureMetadataOutput) expo-camera 57 sets data from AVMetadataMachineReadableCodeObject.stringValue; on Android it uses ML Kit rawValue and falls back to String(rawBytes), so binary payloads are lossy on both platforms. Base64 forces byte mode; digits fit version 2-L (77). The MAC length statement is wrong: RFC 2104 asks for at least half the hash output AND at least 80 bits, which is 128 bits for HMAC-SHA-256; 80 bits is the floor only for SHA-1. NIST SP 800-107r1 calls a 64-bit tag commonly acceptable. Only the server verifies and each student gets one record per session, so 64 bits is defensible, and then the researcher's own 9-byte header plus an 8-byte tag (17 bytes = 136 bits, at most 41 digits) fits version 1-L (41 digits; numeric bitstream 4 + 10 + 137 = 151 of 152 bits). Version 1 is 21 modules, so with the 4-module quiet zone the modules are about 14 percent larger than version 2 on the same screen (29 vs 33 modules).
verdicts.correction: Do not call 80 bits the RFC 2104 minimum. Pick one on purpose: a 128-bit tag (RFC 2104 with SHA-256) gives 61 digits and version 2-L; a 64-bit tag (NIST SP 800-107r1 'commonly acceptable') gives 41 digits and version 1-L, which is what the plan's 'en küçük QR sürümü' asks for.

recommendation_issues.problem: The fallback 'pnpm patch to 1920x1080' may do nothing: with ImageCapture bound in picture mode, the guaranteed YUV size is PREVIEW (screen or 1080p, whichever is smaller), so a budget phone with an HD+ screen can stay near 720p whatever the analyzer asks for. A patch on a core Expo package also has to be redone on every SDK upgrade. Drop the patch as the named remedy; keep the device measurement and the 2x zoom as the first lever, and treat any patch as a last resort with its own regression test.

The 'extra permissions' argument is partly wrong. Location permission is needed anyway (BLE scanning on Android 11 and lower, GPS in Aşama 3). BLUETOOTH_CONNECT is not dead weight: on Android 12+ the system 'turn on Bluetooth' dialog (BluetoothAdapter.ACTION_REQUEST_ENABLE) is annotated @RequiresPermission(BLUETOOTH_CONNECT), and apps targeting API 33+ can no longer enable Bluetooth themselves (enable() always returns false). The own module should still declare and request BLUETOOTH_CONNECT if students and instructors are to get that dialog. The core recommendation (one own module for advertising plus scan-only) stands, but the plan should name react-native-ble-manager as the scanning fallback, matching its own rule that single-maintainer code has a named backup. Source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/Bluetooth/+/refs/heads/main/framework/java/android/bluetooth/BluetoothAdapter.java ('@RequiresBluetoothConnectPermission @RequiresPermission(BLUETOOTH_CONNECT) ... ACTION_REQUEST_ENABLE').

'Android'de sistemin konum servisi' is too loose. A GPS-only read often gives no fix indoors, and NETWORK_PROVIDER 'may require a data connection', which an offline student lacks. The own module should call getCurrentLocation on FUSED_PROVIDER where present (API 31+), else NETWORK then GPS, with a short timeout, and return the accuracy radius and the mock flag. Dropping expo-location also moves permission prompts and iOS authorization into own code, so the effort is larger than the plan's 'küçük yerel kod'; acceptable, but it should be written down. Source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/android14-release/location/java/android/location/LocationManager.java ('Operation of this provider may require a data connection.').

Recommends deferring GPS inside Aşama 3 until trial data shows a need. That re-stages phase content, which the owner excluded from this audit, and it narrows a scope the owner set. Reject the recommendation. The underlying facts (indoor drift, approximate grants, iOS spoofers) are already handled by F10 and by the plan's own rule that GPS is never used alone.

The recommendation is Android-only (UUID mask filter, scan-start quota). An iPhone student cannot filter for a rotating UUID, cannot scan for it in the background, and by default gets one discovery event per peripheral. Without an iPhone rule, the 30 s scan can silently miss the changed code or give a single RSSI sample. Add the iPhone rule from the miss at line 259.

verdict_reason: All 17 findings were re-checked against primary sources: 14 CONFIRMED, 3 CORRECTED (F03 MAC length: RFC 2104 gives 128 bits for SHA-256, and a 64-bit tag allows QR version 1-L; F04 real analysis resolution is capped at PREVIEW size; F07 14 releases on one day, not 13), 0 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. No finding is high severity. Five recommendations need changes (F04 patch, F07 permissions rationale, F08 Android-only, F11 Android provider, F12 out of the owner's bounds). One checked_ok item disputed (line 692 'highest resolution'). Nine misses: three medium (iPhone BLE scanning, the neverForLocation premise of line 261, a stale projected QR on network loss) and six low; none high. The accepted recommendations still remove more dependencies than they add.
